title: Testing the In Vitro and In Vivo Efficiency of mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticles Formulated by Microfluidic Mixing
protocol: Maintain RNase-free conditions when formulating mRNA-LNPs.
Wipe surfaces and equipment with a surface decontaminant for RNases and DNA.
Use only RNase-free tips and reagents.
Fill a clean 4 L beaker with 200-300 mL of fresh 10x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dilute the 10x PBS in the beaker 10-fold with ultrapure water to obtain a beaker of 1x PBS.
Ensure that the final volume of the 1x PBS is between 2-3 L.
Place dialysis cassettes (20 kDa molecular weight cutoff [MWCO]) into the filled beaker to hydrate them.
Hydrate dialysis cassettes for a minimum of 2 min before use.
Place a stir bar into the beaker, and cover the beaker with aluminum foil.
Place the covered beaker onto a magnetic stir plate.
Turn on the stir plate, and set it to spin at 300-400 rpm.
Dilute a 100 mM citric acid buffer stock (pH 3) 10-fold with ultrapure water to create the 10 mM citric acid buffer used for mRNA dilution.
Dissolve C12-200 ionizable lipid, helper lipid, cholesterol, and lipid-PEG in 100% ethanol to make stock solutions.
Heat and mix the stock solutions at 37°C to ensure full dissolution.
Calculate volumes of ionizable lipid, helper lipid, cholesterol, and lipid-PEG based on desired molar ratio and ionizable lipid to mRNA weight ratio.
Combine calculated volumes of different lipid components in a conical tube.
Dilute lipids with 100% ethanol to final volume V representing 25% of the final LNP volume.
Thaw firefly luciferase-encoding mRNA on ice.
Dilute mRNA to a final volume 3V in 10 mM citric acid buffer.
Spray a delicate task wipe with surface decontaminant for RNases and DNA.
Wipe the interior of the microfluidic instrument thoroughly.
Open a new microfluidic cartridge and insert it with inlet channels facing down and away.
Ensure that the conical tube arm holds two 15 mL conical tubes and is positioned furthest to the right.
Configure two sterile 15 mL conical tubes on the holder without caps.
Fill a 5 mL syringe with mRNA solution diluted in 10 mM citric acid buffer.
Fill a 3 mL syringe with lipid solution diluted in pure 100% ethanol.
Flip up the cartridge holder on the microfluidic device.
Insert the 5 mL syringe containing mRNA into the left inlet of the cartridge.
Insert the 3 mL syringe containing lipids into the right inlet of the cartridge.
Flip the cartridge holder back down and close the lid of the microfluidic instrument.
Turn on the microfluidic instrument using the switch located on the back.
Select Quick Run from the interface.
Select the correct syringe types for the 5 mL and 3 mL syringes inserted.
Input parameters for mRNA-LNP formulation at a 3:1 aqueous to organic flow rate ratio as described in Table 2.
Press the Next button to proceed to the next screen.
Confirm that the correct parameters have been inputted.
Press the Start button to formulate the mRNA-LNPs.
Load the mRNA-LNPs collected in the right conical tube into previously hydrated dialysis cassettes.
Do not puncture or damage the membrane of the cassette when loading the mRNA-LNPs.
Place the dialysis cassettes containing the mRNA-LNPs back into the beaker containing 1x PBS.
Leave the dialysis cassettes to dialyze for a minimum of 2 h.
Remove the mRNA-LNPs using a syringe with a needle after dialysis.
Sterile-filter the mRNA-LNPs using a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Collect the filtered mRNA-LNPs in a sterile conical tube.
Place 65 μL of the mRNA-LNP solution into a 1.5 mL microtube for characterization purposes.
Dilute 10 μL of mRNA-LNPs 1:100 in 990 μL of 1x PBS in a cuvette.
Measure the hydrodynamic size and polydispersity index using dynamic light scattering.
Prepare a stock solution of 1x TE buffer by diluting 20x TE buffer with molecular biology water.
Prepare a stock solution of 1% Triton X-100 buffer by diluting Triton X-100 with 1x TE buffer.
Prepare the fluorescent reagent by diluting the reagent stock 1:200 with 1x TE buffer.
Dilute the mRNA-LNPs 1:100 in 1x TE buffer and 1% Triton X-100 buffer in a black-wall black-bottom 96-well plate in 100 μL.
Prepare a low-range standard curve by diluting the RNA standard as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Plate the standard curve in the 96-well plate.
Add 100 µL of diluted fluorescent reagent to each well containing diluted mRNA-LNP or diluted standard.
Place the 96-well plate inside a plate reader.
Shake for 1 min.
Wait for 4 min.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of each well according to the manufacturer's protocol at an excitation/emission of 480 nm/520 nm.
Use the standard curve to convert the fluorescence values to concentrations.
Subtract the value obtained from diluting LNPs in TE buffer (unencapsulated mRNA) from the value obtained from diluting LNPs in 1% Triton X-100 (total mRNA).
Divide by the value obtained from diluting LNPs in 1% Triton X-100 to calculate the encapsulation efficiency.

Subtract the value obtained from diluting LNPs in TE buffer (unencapsulated mRNA) from the value obtained from diluting LNPs in 1% Triton X-100 (total mRNA) to calculate the mRNA-LNP concentration used for cell and animal studies.
Prepare the TNS reagent by creating a 0.16 mM solution of TNS in ultrapure water.
Keep the TNS reagent on ice and away from light to avoid degradation.

Prepare buffered solutions of 150 mM sodium chloride, 20 mM sodium phosphate, 25 mM ammonium citrate, and 20 mM ammonium acetate adjusted to different pH values ranging from 2 to 12 in increments of 0.5.
Add 2.5 μL of LNP to each pH-adjusted buffer solution in a black-wall black-bottom 96-well plate.
Add TNS reagent to each well to achieve a final concentration of 6 µM.
Incubate the 96-well plate in a dark location for 5 minutes.
Measure fluorescence at an excitation/emission wavelength of 322 nm/431 nm using a fluorescence plate reader.
Fit the data to a sigmoidal curve.
Calculate the pKa by finding the pH at which 50% of maximum intensity was observed.

Plate 5,000 HepG2 cells in each well of a white-wall clear-bottom 96-well plate in 100 µL of complete cell culture medium (DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin).
Allow the cells to adhere overnight in a controlled CO2 incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Dilute mRNA-LNPs in complete cell culture medium for a total dose of 100 µL per well.
Remove the complete medium from the wells.
Treat cells with mRNA-LNPs diluted in complete cell culture medium or use complete medium as control.
Incubate the treated 96-well plate containing cells for 24 hours at controlled CO2 conditions.
Prepare luciferase reagent and 1x cell lysis buffer according to manufacturer's instructions.
Remove the cell culture medium from each well of the 96-well plate.
Add 20 µL of 1x lysis buffer to each well.
Add 100 µL of luciferase assay reagent to each well.
Protect the plate from light and place it into a plate reader for bioluminescent signal measurement.
Dilute mRNA-LNP solution with sterile 1x PBS so that 2 µg of total mRNA is present in a 100 µL injection volume.
Restrain each mouse using an approved method.
Wipe the tail with a pad moistened with 70% alcohol.
Fill a 29 G insulin syringe with either 100 µL of mRNA-LNP (2 µg) or 100 µL of 1x PBS.
Remove any bubbles from the syringe.
Insert the needle with the bevel facing up into the mouse's lateral tail vein.
Slowly inject the 100 µL of mRNA-LNP or 1x PBS.
Remove the needle and apply pressure until hemostasis is achieved.
Prepare a stock solution of 15 mg/mL d-luciferin potassium salt in sterile 1x PBS.
Turn on the in vivo imaging system (IVIS).
Open the imaging software.
Press Initialize to prepare the instrument for data acquisition.
Check the box next to luminescence, and set the exposure time to auto.
Ensure that the correct field of view is selected for the number of mice being imaged.
Administer 200 µL of d-luciferin intraperitoneally (150 mg of luciferin per kg body weight) to the previously treated mice.
Place the mice into an anesthesia chamber set to 2.5% isoflurane and an oxygen flowrate of 2.0 L/min.
Wait 10 min for the luciferase signal to stabilize before imaging the mRNA-LNP-treated mice.
Ensure that the mice are fully anesthetized, and redirect the anesthetic line to administer isoflurane via nose cones inside the imaging chamber.
Transfer the mice to the nose cones, ensuring they are on their backs with their abdomens exposed.
Close the chamber door.
Click the Acquire button in the software to obtain bioluminescence images.
